exposure: Mode of birth (vaginal, instrumental, cesarean section)
cohort: 1371 pregnant women with singleton pregnancies at or beyond 24 weeks gestation who completed questionnaires during pregnancy and at two months postpartum.
finding: While skin-to-skin contact after birth was associated with higher birth satisfaction across all modes of birth, the positive effect was particularly pronounced for women who had operative births (instrumental or cesarean).
mod_finding: The association between skin-to-skin contact and birth satisfaction was especially strong for women who had operative births, particularly cesarean sections.
